description: Conformance manifest (ST-5.4, AD-19). Every shipped studio skill MUST have an entry here — the runner discovers surfaces from the plugin's skills/ tree and fails any surface missing from this manifest (and any manifest entry with no shipped skill behind it). Drives run the surface's deterministic core headless in a throwaway sandbox project with an isolated store: stdin closed, wall-clock bounded, output must be machine-readable. argv[0] is plugin-root-relative; {sandbox} substitutes the sandbox project directory.

expect_semantics.json: process completes within the timeout and stdout parses as JSON
expect_semantics.ok: process completes within the timeout, stdout parses as JSON, AND the parsed object carries ok=true — the drive's internal assertions all held (e2e drives whose value is the chain succeeding, not merely answering)
expect_semantics.refusal: process completes within the timeout and refuses cleanly — nonzero exit, JSON with ok=false, or an in-band structured block proven by the declared marker (detect's ask, orchestrate's needs-onboarding) — and when a marker is declared the refusal MUST name it in stdout: an unnamed refusal (a crash, an unrelated error) gives the skill layer nothing to surface as blocked (ISS-002); never a prompt, never a hang

tk-studio-activate.auth_preflight: none needed — read-only local six-plane check (the tracking plane reads the last sync-back's recorded outcome, never the network; the sandbox-login plane reads the engine sandbox's login expiry through a local `sbx exec`, never a token); harness auth is the driver's preflight (driver-contract §1)

tk-studio-install.auth_preflight: npm registry only (npx at the bmad.lock pin) — no Anthropic auth in the surface itself; installer verifies the manifest against the pin after install

tk-studio-base-update.auth_preflight: npm registry (installer rerun at the new pin) + VCS remote for the integration PR; both verified by failing loud, never hanging

tk-studio-detect.auth_preflight: none needed — pure read of the project tree

tk-studio-onboard.auth_preflight: standup + propose/record are local (vault linking skips cleanly when unconfigured); the optional tracking step (plansync.py setup, 0.1.26) refuses before any Atlassian call on an unregistered project or any absent agent-seat variable (TK_ATLASSIAN_SITE on first setup, TK_ATLASSIAN_AGENT_EMAIL, TK_ATLASSIAN_AGENT_TOKEN, TK_ATLASSIAN_AGENT_CONFLUENCE_TOKEN, TK_ATLASSIAN_CLOUD_ID), each named, then proves the agent token through the api.atlassian.com gateway with GET /myself — a 401, the proxy's approval 403 or a scope 403 blocks by name (the sandbox drive below proves the unregistered-project refusal without any network)

tk-studio-launch.auth_preflight: none needed in the surface — the substrate is a local CLI (bmad-loop); the engine's own sessions carry the harness auth preflight (driver-contract §1), and the skill's planner-tier steps run inside the invoking session

the Story 33.5 e2e drive (hole 62): in projects it builds inside the sandbox, launch.py check reconciles the policy's [verify] commands from .tk-studio/config.yaml engine.verify_commands — the tracked command added after the operator's extra, the extra kept, the row and verify_commands key reporting it; a second check unchanged and byte-identical; a project with no tracked list byte-identical

the Story 36.3 e2e drive: track.py's unblock verb refuses in JSON with no binding and no Atlassian call, then bun test test/closeout.test.ts test/sweep.test.ts -t "Story 36.3" from apps/supervisor under a fresh temp folder (the tier-routed re-arm with no host injection, track-unblock once per block, the boundary's end, the bounded stop, the WIP commit), the suite bounded at 240 s and the install at 40 s (below this entry's timeout of 300 s, asserted by the drive); the suite step not run (ok) without the checkout or bun on PATH, the cli_drives precedent

tk-studio-orchestrator.auth_preflight: none needed — stateless read of store + project config

tk-studio-plan-sync.auth_preflight: local backends need none; the jira binding (AD-7) runs the API-token preflight before any backend call — GET /myself proves the token AND the org-admin toggle in one probe, then the issue-type scheme is confirmed against the AD-6 default mapping; unconfigured/unauthenticated runs block named, never a silent 401 (the sandbox drive below proves the block without any network)

drives.note: the Story 35.8 e2e drive: the Stage Log writer through lib/plansync.py stage over a fixture project in a temp folder — --from-pass after dev, review, review (one consult subagent) and the gate to rows dev 1, review 1, review 2, consult 1, gate 1 with the dev row's tokens summed (input + cache-read + cache-creation / output) and priced from prices.json, no elapsed column, the same pass again appended 0; --start before the spec exists buffered in <spec_folder>/stages/<key>.jsonl and flushed by --stop once the spec is written; the supervisor's --append after the engine rows, again appended 0; --stop with no open row a blocked refusal; then the poster (plansync.stage_post) in process over a fake Jira transport (dummy agent-seat variables, no network): a 503 ok:false with the rows unposted, the next run the start and finish comments in AC2's shapes with the [stage:<key> start|stop] marker and one worklog of the derived span, a third run posting nothing

tk-studio-playable-judge.auth_preflight: none needed in the core — playable_judge.py reads report.json and the frames on disk and writes judge.json; the judge session is a routed claude -p leg the supervisor's host leg drives through invokeSkill on the sandbox tier, which carries the harness auth preflight (driver-contract §1)

drives.note: the Story 34.3 e2e drive: the judge's core over a fake judge (a media folder with report.json and frames, a scripted pass answer and a fail answer, judge.json read back, a no-frames refusal), then the host leg's playable step — bun test test/hostverify.test.ts -t "Story 34.3" from apps/supervisor under a fresh temp folder, the suite bounded at 75 s (the drive's worst case — four 4 s core calls, a 12 s install, the 75 s suite — below this entry's timeout: 120, which runner.py honours over its 60 s default, so the drive's own timeouts fire first; hole 97: the Story 34.3 block carries Story 35.3's hardening cases too, 17 tests, about 28 s idle on the agent PC), a fake playable.py runner and a fake judge driving pass, fail, skipped and the refusals; the suite step not run (ok) without the checkout or bun on PATH, the cli_drives precedent

tk-studio-evals.auth_preflight: none needed in the core's drives — evals.py runs the claude CLI it is given (CLAUDE_BIN or --claude-bin; the drives' fake is lib/tests/test_evals.py run as a script); the live claude plugin eval children run on the sandbox tier inside the maintenance-evals worker, whose invokeSkill carries the harness auth preflight (driver-contract §1)

drives.note: the Story 35.5 drive: one claude plugin eval argv per case against a fake claude (lib/tests/test_evals.py run as a script: --version answered, a canned --json result written), scores.json in the output folder and the per-case passes as the status block's reason

gds-engine-godot-4.auth_preflight: none needed — read-only engine knowledge; the core engine_pin.py reads project.godot, global.json and the skill's pin.json on disk and calls nothing (driver-contract §1)

tk-studio-job.auth_preflight: none needed — local run-state reads/writes and substrate directives only; when a run invokes a target skill, that skill's own preflight posture applies (one surface, one preflight)

drives.note: the ST-052 read surface: declared jobs served fully resolved (type extension applied) — what substrate-side recurring classification consumes instead of raw instance files (PROP-008)

the ST-9.4 e2e drive — the run the source lifecycle never had: run-init -> seed -> boundary handoff with deltas -> the wrapper's finish -> queue materialized (deduped on the knowledge.schema.json key) -> routing doc rendered -> the promotion gate opens (ST-9.5: check + dry-run draft walk clean); every step asserted, expect ok means the chain succeeded, not merely answered
the capture verb refuses an unknown run named — never a guess, never a silently empty queue

tk-studio-session.auth_preflight: none needed — local run-workspace reads/writes only; delta validation is pure (lib/knowledge.py)

drives.note: mints the resumable run the boundary drives below split (drives share the sandbox/store and run in order); the timestamped run id is why the session drives select via --job-id

tk-studio-knowledge.auth_preflight: VCS remote + gh only at the push/PR step, both failing loud (a push failure lands the draft commit locally and says so; a gh failure reports the branch as pushed with manual-PR guidance); emit's fetch is best-effort (offline answers from last-fetched refs) — the routing-doc gate, queue read, promoted-baseline dedupe, emission baseline, and sanitization scan are local and need no auth

drives.note: the ST-9.5 refusal drive — a promotion attempt without a rendered routing doc refuses named (the routing doc is the human's promotion-decision surface; D3): a promotion drafted from data no human has seen is not a gated promotion

the ST-9.6 emission verb (D4) — reconciles the promotions record against merged promotion PRs, exactly once per PR; a sandbox with no recorded drafts answers a clean no-op before any git read, never an error

tk-studio-observe.auth_preflight: none needed — local ledger append only

tk-studio-research.auth_preflight: none needed in the deterministic core — charter validation and workspace writes are local; the researching agent's web access rides the harness's own auth (driver-contract §1 preflight)

drives.note: the ST-9.3 seed surface: an invalid artifact refuses named before any run or store read (a knowledge.schema.json-shaped seed against a real run is exercised by the lib suite; intrinsic invalidity is the driver-visible posture)

tk-studio-measure-push.auth_preflight: VCS remote + gh only at the push/PR step, both failing loud (a push failure lands the branch commit locally and says so; a gh failure reports the branch as pushed with manual-PR guidance) — the sanitization re-check and unpushed computation are local and need no auth

tk-studio-consolidate.auth_preflight: none needed — reads the merged measurements/ files and writes issues/ledger.md locally; no network, no backend

tk-studio-evolve.auth_preflight: none needed — reads the merged measurements/ files (and issues/ledger.md as cross-link context) and writes proposals/ledger.md locally; no network, no backend

tk-studio-migrate.auth_preflight: the import step runs the jira adapter's API-token preflight (token + org-admin toggle + issue-type scheme) before any backend write; inventory, verification bookkeeping, and the cutover flag are local — an unconfigured/empty project blocks named before any network (the drives below prove it)

tk-studio-report.auth_preflight: none needed — local ledger append only

tk-studio-track.auth_preflight: the jira binding's agent seat (AD-7), through the planning adapter (AD-4): no planning.jira binding or an absent TK_ATLASSIAN_* variable refuses by name before any call; the adapter's 401/403 split names the token, its email, its expiry, the org toggle, the proxy approval or the scope — never a silent 401 (the sandbox drive below proves the refusal without any network); the `reply` verb (Story 31.6) uses the owner seat instead, host-only (TK_STUDIO_ATLASSIAN_OWNER_EMAIL, TK_STUDIO_ATLASSIAN_OWNER_TOKEN, TK_ATLASSIAN_CLOUD_ID) — an absent owner variable or no binding refuses by name before any call, never posting with another identity (the second drive); the `validate` verb (Story 31.7) uses the agent seat only — no binding or an absent agent variable refuses by name before any call (the third drive)

tk-studio-engage.auth_preflight: none needed — local files only (Story 32.2): `reply` reads the served root's engagement record, chat and memory indexes and appends one line to the engagement's chat.jsonl; no Atlassian, no network, no credential (the planner holds no bearer and no CSRF token, and its session runs with a worker's environment); a missing record refuses by name before anything is written (the drive below proves it)

drives.note: the Story 35.6 e2e drive: engage.closeout in process (stdlib; no bun, no network) in a temp served root with an in-progress engagement record and its scope, two slice stories each with its own leg's report.json, frames and contact sheet (legs/<stamp>/, sheets/<stamp>.png) and the closeout input naming them (slices[].report, frames), against a fake Confluence transport copied into the drive (the shape of test_engage.py's FakeEngagementConfluence, never imported from tests): a complete status block, closeout.md carrying each story's own sheet, its | Report | Value | verdict table and its frame and report links, each file written beside closeout.md with its own leg's bytes, and the page's attachments holding <key>-report.json, every <key>-frame-<name> and the sheets

cli_drives.description: Drives of the meta-CLI (tools/installer/cli), which is not a skill: located from the runner's repository checkout, never the plugin tree; a runner with no checkout beside it records each drive as not run, never a failure. Each runs `python -m <module> <argv>` with TK_STUDIO_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, APPDATA and HOME in a throwaway directory and a PATH holding no claude, sbx or git. {repo} substitutes the checkout root. expect status-block: stdout is exactly one JSON object whose last keys are status, intent, artifacts, reason, and that projection validates against status-block.schema.json with the declared intent (Story 25.5).
